question: How quickly must a personal data breach be reported to the supervisory authority under the GDPR?
evidence: not later than 72 hours after having become aware
expected: Without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of it (Article 33(1) GDPR).

question: What is the maximum administrative fine for the most serious GDPR infringements?
evidence: up to 20 000 000 EUR, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 4 %
note: Article 83(5) GDPR; higher of the two amounts. Fact pattern widened on 2026-11-16 to accept '20,000,000' (see eval/results).
expected: Up to EUR 20 million or, for an undertaking, up to 4% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher (Article 83(5)).

question: What fines can be imposed under the EU AI Act for using a prohibited AI practice?
evidence: EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 %
note: Article 99(3) AI Act as originally published.
expected: Up to EUR 35 million or, for an undertaking, up to 7% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher (Article 99(3)).

question: When do the EU AI Act's obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III start to apply?
evidence: 2 December 2027 for AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6\(2\) and Annex III
note: Original date 2 Aug 2026; moved by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. The flagship 'LLM alone can be out of date' question.
expected: 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems, as moved by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 from the originally published 2 August 2026.

question: From which date do the AI Act's high-risk rules apply to AI systems that are safety components of products covered by EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I)?
evidence: 2 August 2028 for AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6\(1\) and Annex I
expected: 2 August 2028 for high-risk systems under Article 6(1) and Annex I, as set by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

question: What does Article 4 of the AI Act now require from providers and deployers about AI literacy, after the Digital Omnibus on AI?
evidence: take measures to support the development of AI literacy
facts: support the development of AI literacy
note: The original text said 'ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy'; the amendment says 'support the development'.
expected: Article 4 as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 requires providers and deployers to take measures to support the development of AI literacy (the original text said to ensure a sufficient level).

question: Within how many days must a HIPAA covered entity notify affected individuals of a breach of unsecured protected health information?
evidence: no case later than 60 days following the discovery of a breach
expected: Without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 days following the discovery of the breach.

question: How much can a consumer recover in statutory damages per incident when a data breach lets them sue under the CCPA?
evidence: not less than one hundred dollars \(\$100\)\*? and not greater than seven hundred and fifty \(\$750\)
expected: Not less than $100 and not greater than $750 per consumer per incident, or actual damages if greater (Civil Code 1798.150).

question: How long does a controller have to answer a data subject's request to exercise their rights under the GDPR, and can that period be extended?
evidence: within one month of receipt of the request
expected: One month from receipt, extendable by two further months where necessary given complexity and number of requests (Article 12(3)).

question: When does the GDPR restrict decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling?
evidence: right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling
expected: A data subject has the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them (Article 22(1)).

question: Which grounds oblige a controller to erase personal data without undue delay when the data subject asks for it?
evidence: shall have the obligation to erase personal data without undue delay where one of the following grounds applies
expected: Grounds include: data no longer necessary for the purposes, consent withdrawn, successful objection, unlawful processing, legal obligation to erase, data collected from a child (Article 17(1)).

question: Which AI practice does the AI Act prohibit that evaluates or classifies people based on their social behaviour?
evidence: evaluation or classification of natural persons or groups of persons over a certain period of time based on their social behaviour
note: Article 5(1)(c) AI Act. Fact pattern widened on 2026-11-16 to accept 'evaluate or classify' (see eval/results).
expected: Social scoring: evaluating or classifying people over time based on social behaviour or personality characteristics, leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment, is prohibited (Article 5(1)(c)).

question: At what amount of training computation is a general-purpose AI model presumed to have high-impact capabilities under the AI Act?
evidence: floating point operations is greater than 10\^25
expected: When the cumulative training computation is greater than 10^25 floating point operations (Article 51(2)).

question: What training-compute threshold do the Commission's guidelines use to decide whether a model is a general-purpose AI model?
evidence: training compute is greater than 10\^23 FLOP
expected: Training compute greater than 10^23 FLOP and the ability to generate language, text-to-image or text-to-video.

question: What must deployers disclose when an AI system generates or manipulates deep fake content?
evidence: constituting a deep fake, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated
Deployers must disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated
note: Article 50(4) AI Act; Commission transparency guidelines.
expected: Deployers must disclose that the deep fake content has been artificially generated or manipulated (Article 50(4)), with exceptions such as use authorised by law to detect or prevent crime.

question: What are the four functions of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?
evidence: GOVERN.{0,200}MAP.{0,200}MEASURE.{0,200}MANAGE
expected: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage.

question: What are the three steps of the legitimate interest test that the EDPB applies to AI models?
evidence: three-step test that should be conducted when assessing the use of legitimate interest
expected: (1) identify the legitimate interest pursued, (2) analyse the necessity of the processing, (3) assess that the interests or rights of data subjects do not override it (balancing test).

question: How does the GDPR define a controller?
evidence: determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data
determines the purposes and means
expected: The natural or legal person, public authority or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data (Article 4(7)).

question: What are the nine criteria for deciding whether processing is likely to result in a high risk and needs a DPIA?
evidence: following nine criteria should be considered
expected: Evaluation or scoring; automated decision-making with legal or similar effect; systematic monitoring; sensitive or highly personal data; large scale; matching datasets; vulnerable data subjects; innovative use of technology; processing that prevents exercising a right or using a service.

question: Are the Commission's guidelines on classifying high-risk AI systems final or still a draft?
note: Corpus status field: draft. The legal status is printed in the header of every passage of these two documents, so any of their passages is relevant.
expected: They are drafts published for stakeholder consultation, not final guidelines.

question: Compare the breach notification deadlines for the GDPR and the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule.
evidence: not later than 72 hours after having become aware
no case later than 60 days following the discovery of a breach
note: Needs one passage from each regime.
expected: GDPR: without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours of becoming aware, to the supervisory authority. HIPAA: to affected individuals without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery.

question: Do both the GDPR and the California CCPA give people a right to have their personal data deleted?
evidence: shall have the obligation to erase personal data without undue delay where one of the following grounds applies
right to request that a business delete any personal information about the consumer
note: Article 17 GDPR and Civil Code 1798.105; needs one passage from each.
expected: Yes: Article 17 GDPR gives a right to erasure, and CCPA Civil Code 1798.105 gives consumers the right to request deletion of personal information a business collected from them.

question: Can companies rely on legitimate interest to scrape web data for training generative AI, according to the EDPB?
evidence: legitimate interest \(Article 6\(1\)\(f\) GDPR\) is often used by private entities for scraping
expected: Legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f)) is often used for scraping, but it applies lawfully only if the conditions of the three-part test (legitimate interest, necessity, balancing) are met.

question: What deadline does Brazil's LGPD set for notifying a data breach?
note: Brazil is not covered by any of the 34 documents.
expected: The documents do not cover this. The answer should say so instead of answering.

question: What penalties does the Colorado AI Act impose on developers of high-risk AI systems?
note: Colorado appears only in bibliographies; the Act itself is not in the corpus.
expected: The documents do not cover this. The answer should say so instead of answering.
